acceptedEdits.originalParagraph: Toren went through his father's coat because somebody had to and because he could not stand to have somebody else do it. There was: a folding knife. A flint. Three feet of waxed cord. Two dried apples. A bone comb that had been his mother's, which Toren had not known his father carried and which was the thing that finally broke him, out of everything, a comb. A folded paper with the Coldwater bridge tolls written on it in his father's blocky hand, and under that a column of numbers that Toren looked at for a while before he understood: days. His father had been counting the days to Meridian against something. Against Senna, probably. Against the road.

acceptedEdits.originalParagraph: "She can't walk," Dessa said. "She rides, which means the cart goes, which means the cart goes at a mule's pace with one wheel that's already broken once today. There's four of us. One Ember and he got it this morning. A bar and a shovel. No shells. And that stuff you're pouring in your flask —" she pointed at the seams in the road bed, at the long grey slick of it "— that's a smell, isn't it. That's why you're taking it up. It brings more."
